title: Tata Technologies Ltd - 544028 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 12.4% QoQ in constant currency to INR 1,572 crores, with EBITDA margin at 16%; management guides to double-digit organic FY27 growth.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered on prior guidance of over 10% sequential revenue growth and an operating margin above 16%. Total revenue was INR 1,572 crores (+12.4% QoQ constant currency), of which about 8 points was organic and about 4 points came from ES-Tec, which was consolidated for a full three months versus one month in Q3. EBITDA rose 30.7% QoQ to INR 252 crores at a 16% margin, and a INR 56 crore reversal of the labour code provision lifted reported profit. Management reiterated double-digit organic constant-currency growth for FY27 and an exit FY27 operating margin above 18%.

segments.name: Automotive
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 13.6% QoQ in USD terms, driven by both anchor and non-anchor clients; management says non-anchor customers grew meaningfully faster. JLR has returned to its pre-cyber-attack run rate.

segments.name: Aerospace and Industrial Heavy Machinery
segments.commentary: Grew 4.6% QoQ. Aerospace annual run rate is above $40 million, up 8x over four years; Airbus (EMES3 program) is a flagship account, with Air India MRO and North American engine makers also contributing.

segments.commentary: Revenue of INR 353 crores, up 12% QoQ; Education business grew 36-40% QoQ.

segments.commentary: Declined 10% QoQ after a seasonally strong Q3, reflecting normal phasing of customer PLM budgets.

segments.name: Embedded Software
segments.commentary: Revenue has grown at a 60% CAGR over the last three years, per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 organic constant-currency revenue growth guided at double digits, excluding ES-Tec inorganic contribution; management says growth is expected in both anchor and non-anchor automotive clients.
Exit FY27 operating margin run rate above 18%, driven by volume-led operating leverage, offshore and pyramid mix, and AI-driven unit-cost reduction.

Management expects H2 FY27 growth to be faster than H1, with consistency across all four quarters; guidance excludes any demand improvement and is based on order book and probability-adjusted pipeline.
Middle East crisis: management expects discretionary spend to tighten if it persists, but says capex and new-product commitments are unaffected and the double-digit guidance is factored in.
ES-Tec: Q4 contribution about $9 million; management expects roughly $11-12 million in total across the partial prior month and Q4. Post-merger integration said to be on track.
Long-term North Star revenue target of $1 billion, with management expecting to get there within 2-3 years, potentially aided by one or two inorganic deals.
capex_capacity: Capacity was deliberately retained through the downturn; headcount added only 66 in Q4, and hiring will remain selective and focused on strategic areas.
Growing talent ahead of expected FY27 wins; volume growth is cited as the main margin lever.
More than 50% of the engineering workforce is now AI-ready; TechVarsity delivered 796+ modules to 11,000+ employees (about 85% of the workforce).
Proprietary AI platform Chromosome AI is being used as an orchestration layer across product development, with AI deployed across all delivery lines and enabling functions.
demand_pricing: Four large deals closed in Q4: a North American commercial vehicle OEM (PLM, testing and QA, MES, project management); a European automotive OEM on comfort electronics; a European OEM partnership on supplier quality; and a multi-year Tier 1 engagement to superscale a global engineering centre.
Two milestone wins in April 2026: a European luxury automotive OEM (enterprise PLM transformation and operations) and a Full-Vehicle Program with a leading Japanese OEM, marking entry into Japan.
Two Full-Vehicle Programs closed in Q3 and Q4; at least two more are expected to close in the next 8-12 weeks. Programs run 18-36 months with deal values in the tens of millions of dollars.
Top 20 customers make up about 88% of business.
Tariff-related deferrals in FY25 and H1 FY26 are said to be easing; management reports improving decision velocity at OEMs.
German OEMs are described as reticent to use India-based providers; management is in advanced discussions with OEMs and Tier 1s in Germany about India delivery.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 12% QoQ growth was organic, and how durable is it? What is the JLR position after the cyber-attack?
qa_highlights.answer: Of the 12%, about 8 points was organic and about 4 points ES-Tec, as planned. JLR has returned to its pre-cyber-attack run rate, and new deals were won with both anchor and non-Tata automotive accounts.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue and cost synergies are expected from ES-Tec, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Integration is on track and the business plan is being delivered, with business already won at VW. Synergies are being pursued through cross-selling into VW and extending services to the existing customer base, with proof points already in hand.

qa_highlights.question: What powertrains are in the full-vehicle wins, and what drives the turnaround after EV write-downs at OEMs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is propulsion-agnostic (ICE, PHEV, range-extender, BEV). It sees latent demand for new products that was deferred during tariff uncertainty now being released, and says the Japanese full-vehicle win validates its value proposition.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Middle East crisis affecting client spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects discretionary spend could tighten if the crisis persists, through aluminium and plastics supply and pricing effects. It does not expect capex or new-product commitments to be affected, and says the impact is in guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did BMW JV profit share dip, and what is the margin bridge from 16% to 18%?
qa_highlights.answer: The dip to INR 6.6 crores was a one-quarter year-end true-up, and the JV is expected to return to its prior run rate. The margin bridge relies on volume-led operating leverage, offshore and pyramid mix, and AI-driven unit-cost reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 double-digit growth in constant currency or in USD or INR, and how does it phase through the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is in constant currency. Management expects consistency across quarters, with H2 growing faster than H1 because of deals expected to close in the next 4-6 weeks.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict: commodity (aluminium, plastics) supply and pricing could tighten OEM discretionary spend.
Ramp of full-vehicle programs (at least two more expected to close in 8-12 weeks) and whether H2-weighted growth materialises.
Sustainability of organic growth beyond the 8.8% Q4 print, given JLR recovery and Products decline of 10% QoQ.
ES-Tec integration and cross-sell into VW, given European OEM write-downs and headwinds.
Attrition at 16.2% and rising, while headcount is only growing slowly.
Labour code provision reversal (INR 56 crores) is a one-time item; Q3 INR 140 crore charge indicates the reported profit trajectory is noisy.
FY27 margin path to above 18% exit requires about 200 bps further expansion from the 16% Q4 level.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the FY27 outlook and the Q4 inflection, with specific deal and pipeline detail. Cautious on the Middle East impact on client discretionary spend, which management says is already in guidance. Evasive on the composition of the margin walk beyond volume, offshore mix and AI.
key_quotes: Q4 was not just a strong finish to the year - it represents a turning point.
we are very confident that what we established in Q4 represents a platform from which we can go on and deliver the double-digit organic growth that we previously committed to.
I fully expect discretionary spend amongst our customers to tighten if the Middle East crisis continues to extend.
we expect to exit FY27 with an operating margin run rate that exceeds 18%

growth.why: Management reiterated double-digit organic cc revenue growth for FY27 (ex ES-Tec), backed by order book and probability-adjusted pipeline, four large Q4 deal wins and two more full-vehicle programs expected in 8-12 weeks; no new physical capacity added and capex/capacity not discussed, so backing is partial.
